card.law_is_about: Detailed implementation of revised emissions-trading rules, including sustainability evidence for biomass.
card.they_want: Introduce grandfathering or a transition period, with the 80% requirement no earlier than 2027.
card.they_claim: Every biomass plant in EU ETS 1 must demonstrate 80% greenhouse-gas savings from 1 January 2026.
card.the_problem: The addressed rules retain commissioning-date and operating-age distinctions, including 70% for a 2021–2023 cohort until 2029.

locator.section: Table 1, installations ≥10 MW, start between 1 January 2021 and 20 November 2023; first two lines of the relevant table cell.

correction: Replace the universal immediate 80% description with the applicable commissioning-date and operating-age cohorts. The exact draft § 3(3) preserves the relevant start date and years of biomass use; its explanation physical 34 says older plants roll into the 80% requirement after 15 years. Pre-submission Commission guidance table 1 expressly gives 70% until 31 December 2029 for biomass-fuel installations ≥10 MW starting between 1 January 2021 and 20 November 2023, followed by 80% from 2030. Newer plants and certain older cohorts can indeed face 80% in 2026.
effect: Narrows the breadth and immediacy of the asserted burden supporting a general transition request.
limits: This does not establish that affected old plants face no immediate burden, that compliance supplies are readily available, or that a transition is unnecessary. Optional grandfathering under Article 29(15) and automatic cohort thresholds under Article 29(10) are distinct; the finding does not resolve the acknowledged legal debate over applying the former in EU ETS 1. No conclusion about actual E.ON fleet composition or total affected capacity is drawn.
context_and_alternatives: Both author pages were read, including page 2 expressly acknowledging uncertainty over EU ETS applicability of Article 29(15). That acknowledgement concerns the optional extra grandfathering route; it does not convert Article 29(10) into a universal 80% threshold.

A benign reading could mean all plants in a narrower affected older cohort or all E.ON assets of interest. No such portfolio or operating-age restriction accompanies the challenged all-plants sentence. The surrounding description instead speaks generally about biomass installations falling into EU ETS through site aggregation.

The draft explanation directly confirms different applicable criteria depending on commissioning date. The counterexample is an express legal cohort, not merely the absence of evidence that all existing installations are affected.
Commission guidance is an official but non-binding explanation of the EU rules. The exact national draft is the principal version check; later adopted regulation is not substituted.
The short claim quote isolates the universal quantifier; the full continuation naming 1 January 2026 and 80% was read and visually checked at the same precise locator.

The prior August 2025 BioSt-NachV consultation draft, physical 10–11 proposed § 6(2), also contains 70% for the 2021–2023 cohort and operating-age distinctions for older plants. It separately proposes optional extra grandfathering in § 6(4), confirming that these are distinct layers. This EEG-focused draft corroborates context and is not substituted for the addressed EHV draft.
